review.notes: Ataúro 2016 survey (Conservation International Rapid Assessment, July 2016, 10 sites): average 253 species per site, previous record 216 (Raja Ampat), richest site 315, total about 642–643 species (Mongabay, Reef Builders); a 2012 national survey reported 294 species at one Ataúro site. Cetaceans: Charles Darwin University study 2016–2023, at least 21 species (one other source says 24 for the strait); ANU: more than 2,700 blue-whale sightings since 2014; whale season about October–December (tourism sources). Coral Triangle 'about three-quarters (76%) of known coral species' – general reference. Turtles: 'rare and need protection' (legal status not checked). Tetun terms to check: kima (giant clam), tubaraun, mergulladór, baleia kaxalote, baleia ulun-melaun, boek, kadiuk (crab), bubu (fish trap), ahu-ruin sai mutin (bleaching).

title.tet: Lafaek tasi nian
title.pt: O crocodilo-de-água-salgada (lafaek)
title.en: The saltwater crocodile (lafaek)
title.id: Buaya muara (lafaek)

summary.tet: Lafaek tasi nian mak réptil boot liu ne'ebé moris iha mundu. Timoroan barak respeita nia hanesan bei'ala no bolu nia “avó” (Avó Lafaek), no ai-knanoik famozu ida dehan katak illa Timór uluk mak lafaek ida. Maibé lafaek mós animál fuik perigozu, tan ne'e ema tenke kuidadu besik mota, lagoa no tasi-ibun.
summary.pt: O crocodilo-de-água-salgada, lafaek em tétum, é o maior réptil vivo. Muitos timorenses respeitam-no como antepassado e chamam-lhe «avô» (Avô Lafaek), e uma lenda famosa diz que a ilha de Timor foi em tempos um crocodilo. É também um animal selvagem perigoso, por isso é preciso ter cuidado perto de rios, pântanos e praias.
summary.en: The saltwater crocodile, lafaek in Tetun, is the largest living reptile. Many Timorese respect it as an ancestor and call it “grandfather” (Avô Lafaek), and a famous legend says that the island of Timor was once a crocodile. It is also a dangerous wild animal, so people must stay safe near rivers, swamps and beaches.
summary.id: Buaya muara, yang dalam bahasa Tetun disebut lafaek, adalah reptil hidup terbesar. Banyak orang Timor menghormatinya sebagai leluhur dan menyebutnya “kakek” (Avô Lafaek), dan sebuah legenda terkenal mengatakan bahwa Pulau Timor dahulu adalah seekor buaya. Buaya juga hewan liar yang berbahaya, sehingga orang harus berhati-hati di dekat sungai, rawa, dan pantai.

text.tet: Lafaek tasi nian (Crocodylus porosus) moris husi Índia no Sudeste Aziátiku to'o Nova Giné no Austrália nia norte. Nia mak réptil boot liu ne'ebé sei moris ohin loron. Lafaek mane boot bele naruk liu metru 5 no, dala uitoan, to'o maizumenus metru 6, maibé lafaek feto ki'ik liu, dala barak maizumenus metru 3. Nia moris iha bee mota nian, bee kahur no bee-tasi, no bele nani dook iha kosta naruk no liu tasi luan. Iha Timór-Leste ita hetan nia iha mota-ibun, lagoa, fatin bokon, ai-parapa no iha tasi-ibun balu, iha kosta norte no kosta sul.
text.pt: O crocodilo-de-água-salgada ou crocodilo-marinho (Crocodylus porosus) vive desde a Índia e o Sudeste Asiático até à Nova Guiné e ao norte da Austrália. É o maior réptil vivo. Os machos grandes podem passar dos 5 m e, raramente, chegar a cerca de 6 m, enquanto as fêmeas são mais pequenas, muitas vezes com cerca de 3 m. Vive em água doce, salobra e salgada e consegue nadar longas distâncias ao longo das costas e em mar aberto. Em Timor-Leste encontra-se em fozes de rios, lagoas, pântanos e mangais e junto a algumas praias, tanto na costa norte como na costa sul.
text.en: The saltwater or estuarine crocodile (Crocodylus porosus) lives from India and Southeast Asia to New Guinea and northern Australia. It is the largest reptile alive today. Large males can grow to more than 5 m and, rarely, to about 6 m, while females are smaller, often around 3 m. It lives in fresh, brackish and salt water and can swim long distances along coasts and across the open sea. In Timor-Leste it is found in river mouths, lagoons, swamps and mangroves and along some beaches, on both the north and the south coast.
text.id: Buaya muara (Crocodylus porosus) hidup dari India dan Asia Tenggara sampai Papua dan Australia bagian utara. Hewan ini adalah reptil terbesar yang masih hidup. Buaya jantan besar bisa tumbuh lebih dari 5 m dan, meski jarang, sampai sekitar 6 m, sedangkan betinanya lebih kecil, sering sekitar 3 m. Buaya muara hidup di air tawar, payau, dan asin, serta dapat berenang jauh menyusuri pantai dan menyeberangi laut lepas. Di Timor-Leste buaya ini ditemukan di muara sungai, laguna, rawa, hutan bakau, dan di beberapa pantai, baik di pesisir utara maupun selatan.

text.tet: Lafaek iha fatin espesiál iha kultura timoroan. Família barak haree lafaek hanesan bei'ala no bolu nia avó — Avó Lafaek. Ai-knanoik ne'ebé famozu liu konta kona-ba lafaek ki'ik ida ne'ebé labarik-mane ida salva. Atu hatudu agradesimentu, lafaek lori labarik ne'e liu tasi sira, no bainhira nia sai katuas, nia sai illa Timór, no ninia kotuk sai foho sira. Tan ne'e, ba ema barak lafaek mak lulik, no halo aat ba lafaek dala barak bandu. Lafaek mós fó naran ba revista aprendizajen labarik nian Lafaek, no ba aplikasaun Lafa ne'e.
text.pt: Os crocodilos têm um lugar especial na cultura timorense. Muitas famílias veem o crocodilo como um antepassado e chamam-lhe, com respeito, Avô Lafaek, o «Avô Crocodilo». A lenda mais conhecida conta a história de um pequeno crocodilo salvo por um rapaz; em agradecimento, levou-o pelos mares e, quando ficou velho, transformou-se na ilha de Timor, e as suas costas tornaram-se as montanhas. Por isso, para muitas pessoas os crocodilos são lulik (sagrados), e fazer-lhes mal é muitas vezes tabu. O crocodilo deu também o nome à Lafaek, uma revista de aprendizagem para crianças, e a esta aplicação Lafa.
text.en: Crocodiles have a special place in Timorese culture. Many families see the crocodile as an ancestor and respectfully call it Avô Lafaek, “Grandfather Crocodile”. The best-known legend tells of a small crocodile saved by a boy; in thanks it carried him across the seas, and when it grew old it turned into the island of Timor, its back becoming the mountains. Crocodiles are therefore lulik (sacred) for many people, and harming one is often taboo. The crocodile also gave its name to Lafaek, a children's learning magazine, and to this Lafa app.
text.id: Buaya punya tempat istimewa dalam budaya Timor. Banyak keluarga memandang buaya sebagai leluhur dan dengan hormat memanggilnya Avô Lafaek, “Kakek Buaya”. Legenda yang paling terkenal bercerita tentang buaya kecil yang diselamatkan seorang anak laki-laki; sebagai tanda terima kasih buaya itu membawanya menyeberangi lautan, dan ketika menjadi tua ia berubah menjadi Pulau Timor, dan punggungnya menjadi pegunungan. Karena itu bagi banyak orang buaya bersifat lulik (sakral), dan menyakitinya sering dianggap pantang. Buaya juga menjadi nama Lafaek, majalah belajar untuk anak-anak, dan nama aplikasi Lafa ini.

text.tet: Respeitu la hasai perigu. Lafaek tasi nian mak animál ne'ebé kasa makaas no bele ataka ema iha bee ninin. Peskizadór sira hetan katak lafaek ataka ema beibeik liu iha Timór-Leste desde maizumenus 2007. Iha estudu ida kona-ba atake sira entre 2007 no 2021, vítima barak liu mak mane no labarik-mane, besik parte tolu husi haat mak peskadór, no atake barak liu halo ema mate. Atu seguru: keta nani, hariis ka fase roupa iha fatin ne'ebé lafaek hela; hela dook husi bee ninin; kuidadu liu iha dadeer-saan, loro-monu no kalan; nunka fó hahán ba lafaek; no tuir sinál avizu sira. Labarik sira tenke ho ema boot beibeik bainhira besik mota no lagoa.
text.pt: O respeito não elimina o perigo. Os crocodilos-de-água-salgada são caçadores poderosos que podem atacar pessoas à beira da água. Os investigadores verificaram que os ataques em Timor-Leste se tornaram muito mais frequentes a partir de cerca de 2007. Num estudo dos ataques entre 2007 e 2021, a maioria das vítimas eram homens e rapazes, quase três quartos eram pescadores e a maior parte dos ataques foi mortal. Para estar seguro: não nade, não tome banho nem lave roupa onde vivem crocodilos; fique bem afastado da beira da água; tenha mais cuidado ao amanhecer, ao anoitecer e à noite; nunca dê comida aos crocodilos; e respeite os sinais de aviso. As crianças devem estar sempre com adultos perto de rios e lagoas.
text.en: Respect does not remove danger. Saltwater crocodiles are powerful hunters that can attack people at the water's edge. Researchers found that attacks in Timor-Leste became much more frequent from about 2007. In a study of attacks between 2007 and 2021, most victims were men and boys, nearly three-quarters were fishers, and most attacks were fatal. To stay safe: do not swim, bathe or wash clothes where crocodiles live; stay well back from the water's edge; take extra care at dawn, dusk and night; never feed crocodiles; and follow warning signs. Children should always be with adults near rivers and lagoons.
text.id: Rasa hormat tidak menghilangkan bahaya. Buaya muara adalah pemburu kuat yang dapat menyerang orang di tepi air. Para peneliti menemukan bahwa serangan buaya di Timor-Leste menjadi jauh lebih sering sejak sekitar 2007. Dalam penelitian tentang serangan antara 2007 dan 2021, sebagian besar korban adalah laki-laki dan anak laki-laki, hampir tiga perempatnya nelayan, dan sebagian besar serangan berakibat fatal. Agar aman: jangan berenang, mandi, atau mencuci pakaian di tempat buaya hidup; menjauhlah dari tepi air; lebih waspada saat fajar, senja, dan malam; jangan pernah memberi makan buaya; dan patuhi tanda peringatan. Anak-anak harus selalu didampingi orang dewasa di dekat sungai dan laguna.

text.tet: Iha Timór-Leste, lei proteje lafaek desde 2000. Iha fatin seluk iha rejiaun ne'e, ema kasa lafaek barak iha sékulu 20 atu foti sira-nia kulit, no ohin loron CITES kontrola komérsiu internasionál kulit lafaek nian. Tanba lafaek mak lulik, ema barak la hakarak oho lafaek maski hafoin atake ida, no atake balu ema la relata. Peskizadór balu hanoin katak lafaek boot balu karik nani mai Timór husi Austrália, fatin ne'ebé lafaek sira aumenta ona, maibé seidauk iha prova. Autoridade no komunidade sira buka solusaun hamutuk: sinál avizu, fatin seguru atu foti bee, hanorin labarik sira, no muda lafaek perigozu ba fatin seluk bainhira presiza.
text.pt: Em Timor-Leste, os crocodilos estão protegidos por lei desde 2000. Noutros lugares da região foram muito caçados no século XX por causa da pele, e o comércio internacional de peles de crocodilo é hoje controlado pela CITES. Como os crocodilos são lulik, muitas pessoas não querem que sejam mortos mesmo depois de um ataque, e alguns ataques não são comunicados. Alguns investigadores sugeriram que certos crocodilos grandes podem nadar da Austrália, onde o seu número aumentou, até Timor, mas isso não está provado. As autoridades e as comunidades procuram soluções em conjunto: sinais de aviso, lugares seguros para buscar água, ensino às crianças e, quando necessário, a remoção de crocodilos perigosos.
text.en: In Timor-Leste, crocodiles have been protected by law since 2000. Elsewhere in the region they were hunted heavily in the 20th century for their skins, and international trade in crocodile skins is now controlled through CITES. Because crocodiles are lulik, many people do not want them killed even after an attack, and some attacks are never reported. Researchers have suggested that some large crocodiles may swim to Timor from Australia, where their numbers have grown, but this is not proven. Authorities and communities look for solutions together: warning signs, safe places to collect water, teaching children, and moving dangerous crocodiles when needed.
text.id: Di Timor-Leste, buaya dilindungi undang-undang sejak tahun 2000. Di tempat lain di kawasan ini, buaya banyak diburu pada abad ke-20 untuk diambil kulitnya, dan kini perdagangan internasional kulit buaya diatur melalui CITES. Karena buaya dianggap lulik, banyak orang tidak ingin buaya dibunuh bahkan setelah terjadi serangan, dan sebagian serangan tidak dilaporkan. Para peneliti menduga sebagian buaya besar mungkin berenang ke Timor dari Australia, tempat jumlahnya meningkat, tetapi hal ini belum terbukti. Pemerintah dan masyarakat bersama-sama mencari jalan keluar: tanda peringatan, tempat aman untuk mengambil air, pendidikan bagi anak-anak, dan memindahkan buaya berbahaya bila perlu.

review.notes: Respectful name: the earlier Lafa culture article uses 'avó' (grandparent); the brief asks for 'Avô Lafaek'. Check the preferred Tetun form (avó / abó) and whether 'Avô Lafaek' is the usual phrase; research also mentions the 'Lafaek Diak' (Good Crocodile) creation myth and the crocodile's lulik status. Legal protection since 2000 comes from an idw press release (probably UNTAET Regulation 2000/19) – check. Attack figures: Lakehead University study summary for 2007–2021 (84% male, 73% fishers, 43% under 20, about 70% fatal); another study (130 attacks 1996–2014, 52% fatal) shows a sharp rise after 2007. 'Crocodiles from Australia' is a hypothesis. Quiz 1 asks for the meaning of lafaek in each reader's language (in Tetun, the English word). summary.tet: Timór iha mamíferu naturál uitoan de'it, tanba tasi kle'an hadook sira barak. Niki, laho, manu no réptil mai rasik, maibé bibi-rusa, lekirauk, kuskus no animál hakiak barak, ema mak lori mai uluk liu. Ohin loron kuda Timór no karau sai parte husi moris loron-loron no kultura.
summary.pt: Timor tem poucos mamíferos nativos, porque mares profundos mantiveram a maioria afastada. Morcegos, ratos, aves e répteis chegaram sozinhos, enquanto veados, macacos, cuscos e muitos animais de criação foram trazidos por pessoas há muito tempo. Hoje o pónei de Timor e o búfalo fazem parte da vida diária e da cultura.
summary.en: Timor has few native mammals, because deep seas kept most of them away. Bats, rats, birds and reptiles arrived by themselves, while deer, macaques, cuscus and many farm animals were brought by people long ago. Today the Timor pony and the water buffalo are part of daily life and culture.
summary.id: Timor hanya memiliki sedikit mamalia asli, karena laut dalam menghalangi sebagian besar mamalia. Kelelawar, tikus, burung, dan reptil datang sendiri, sedangkan rusa, monyet, kuskus, dan banyak hewan ternak dibawa oleh manusia sejak lama. Kini kuda timor dan kerbau menjadi bagian dari kehidupan sehari-hari dan budaya.

text.tet: Tanba tasi kle'an fahe Timór husi Ázia no Austrália beibeik, animál ne'ebé bele semo, nani ka namlele liu tasi de'it mak to'o rasik. Tan ne'e mak Timór nia mamíferu naturál tuan liu mak niki no laho. Fósil hatudu katak uluk Timór iha laho boot sira no elefante nia família ki'ik ida, Stegodon, maibé sira lakon ona. Réptil barak moris iha ne'e, hanesan teki no samea, no lagartu ida naran varanu Timór ne'ebé ki'ik; anfíbiu balu mós moris iha ne'e. Lafaek tasi nian to'o illa ne'e ho nani.
text.pt: Como Timor esteve sempre separada da Ásia e da Austrália por águas profundas, só chegaram sozinhos os animais que conseguiam voar, nadar ou ser levados pelo mar. Por isso, os mamíferos nativos mais antigos de Timor são os morcegos e os ratos. Os fósseis mostram que Timor teve ratos gigantes e um pequeno parente dos elefantes, o Stegodon, mas estão extintos. Vivem cá muitos répteis, como osgas, lagartixas, cobras e o pequeno varano-de-timor, e também rãs. O crocodilo-de-água-salgada chegou à ilha a nadar.
text.en: Because Timor was always cut off from Asia and Australia by deep water, only animals that could fly, swim or drift across the sea arrived on their own. That is why Timor's oldest native mammals are bats and rats. Fossils show that Timor once had giant rats and a small elephant relative, Stegodon, but these are extinct. Many reptiles live here, such as geckos, skinks, snakes and the small Timor monitor lizard, as well as frogs. The saltwater crocodile reached the island by swimming.
text.id: Karena Timor selalu terpisah dari Asia dan Australia oleh laut dalam, hanya hewan yang bisa terbang, berenang, atau hanyut menyeberangi laut yang datang sendiri. Itulah sebabnya mamalia asli tertua di Timor adalah kelelawar dan tikus. Fosil menunjukkan bahwa Timor pernah memiliki tikus raksasa dan kerabat kecil gajah, yaitu Stegodon, tetapi keduanya sudah punah. Banyak reptil hidup di sini, seperti tokek, kadal, ular, dan biawak timor yang kecil, serta katak. Buaya muara sampai ke pulau ini dengan berenang.

text.tet: Durante tinan rihun barak, ema ne'ebé mai Timór ho ró lori animál sira hamutuk, ho intensaun ka la ho intensaun. Sientista sira hanoin katak bibi-rusa (Rusa timorensis) mai husi Java no Bali, lekirauk husi illa sira iha oeste, no kuskus — animál ida ne'ebé hela iha ai leten, la'o neineik no hakiak oan iha ninia kabun nia bolsa — mai husi Maluku. Fahi, asu, bibi, manu no laku (musang) mós ema mak lori mai. Ohin loron bibi-rusa no lekirauk moris fuik iha ai-laran, no ema sei kasa balu; kasa tenke tuir lei no regra lisan nian.
text.pt: Ao longo de milhares de anos, as pessoas que navegavam para Timor trouxeram animais, de propósito ou por acaso. Os cientistas pensam que o veado-de-timor (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa em tétum) veio de Java e Bali, o macaco-de-cauda-longa (lekirauk) das ilhas a oeste, e o cusco — um marsupial lento que vive nas árvores, parente dos opossuns australianos — das Molucas. Porcos, cães, cabras, galinhas e a civeta-das-palmeiras também foram trazidos por pessoas. Hoje os veados e os macacos vivem em liberdade nas florestas, e alguns ainda são caçados, o que deve respeitar a lei e as regras tradicionais.
text.en: Over thousands of years, people sailing to Timor brought animals with them, on purpose or by accident. Scientists think the Timor deer (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa in Tetun) came from Java and Bali, the long-tailed macaque (lekirauk) from the islands to the west, and the common cuscus — a slow, tree-living marsupial related to Australian possums — from the Moluccas. Pigs, dogs, goats, chickens and the palm civet were also brought by people. Today deer and macaques live wild in the forests, and some are still hunted, which must respect the law and customary rules.
text.id: Selama ribuan tahun, orang yang berlayar ke Timor membawa hewan, sengaja atau tidak sengaja. Ilmuwan menduga rusa timor (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa dalam bahasa Tetun) berasal dari Jawa dan Bali, monyet ekor panjang (lekirauk) dari pulau-pulau di sebelah barat, dan kuskus — hewan berkantung yang lamban dan hidup di pohon, kerabat posum Australia — dari Maluku. Babi, anjing, kambing, ayam, dan musang luwak juga dibawa manusia. Kini rusa dan monyet hidup liar di hutan, dan sebagian masih diburu, yang harus mematuhi hukum dan aturan adat.

text.tet: Kuda Timór mak kuda ki'ik ida ne'ebé forte no la'o di'ak iha dalan susar. Durante sékulu barak, kuda mak dalan prinsipál atu la'o no lori sasán iha foho nia dalan ki'ik ne'ebé tun-sa'e, no ema sei uza nia iha área rurál, iha serimónia no iha halai-kuda. Iha sékulu 19, ema lori kuda Timór ho ró ba Austrália no fatin seluk, no iha ne'ebá sira influensia kuda lokál sira. Kuda mós mosu iha timoroan nia istória no hananu, no iha rejiaun balu kuda parte husi sasán ne'ebé família sira fó malu iha barlake.
text.pt: O pónei de Timor (kuda em tétum) é um cavalo pequeno, forte e de passo seguro. Durante séculos foi o principal meio de viajar e de transportar cargas nos caminhos íngremes das montanhas, e ainda é usado nas zonas rurais, em cerimónias e corridas. No século XIX, os póneis de Timor foram levados de barco para a Austrália e outros lugares, onde influenciaram raças locais. Os cavalos aparecem também em histórias e canções timorenses e, em algumas regiões, fazem parte das trocas de casamento (barlake).
text.en: The Timor pony (kuda in Tetun) is a small, strong and sure-footed horse. For centuries it was the main way to travel and carry loads on steep mountain paths, and it is still used in rural areas and at ceremonies and races. In the 19th century Timor ponies were shipped to Australia and other places, where they influenced local breeds. Horses also appear in Timorese stories and songs, and in some regions they are part of the gifts exchanged at marriages (barlake).
text.id: Kuda timor (kuda dalam bahasa Tetun) adalah kuda kecil yang kuat dan langkahnya mantap. Selama berabad-abad kuda ini menjadi sarana utama untuk bepergian dan mengangkut barang di jalan setapak pegunungan yang curam, dan masih dipakai di pedesaan, dalam upacara, dan pacuan. Pada abad ke-19 kuda timor dikirim ke Australia dan tempat lain, tempat kuda ini memengaruhi ras setempat. Kuda juga muncul dalam cerita dan lagu Timor, dan di beberapa daerah menjadi bagian dari pertukaran perkawinan (barlake).

text.tet: Karau mak animál hakiak ne'ebé iha folin boot liu iha Timór-Leste nia fatin barak. Karau mak sinál riku-soin nian: ema fó karau iha barlake no oho karau iha serimónia importante, hanesan mate-rate no inaugurasaun uma lulik. Iha natar balu, agrikultór sira tuir tradisaun dada karau liu natar ne'ebé nakonu ho bee atu sama no prepara rai. Baka Bali, bibi no fahi mós barak, no família barak hakiak manu. Animál sira dala barak la'o livre, no ida-ne'e bele estraga to'os no ai-oan sira, tan ne'e komunidade sira halo regra kona-ba fatin ne'ebé animál bele han du'ut.
text.pt: O búfalo-de-água (karau em tétum) é o animal de criação mais valioso em muitas partes de Timor-Leste. Os búfalos são sinal de riqueza: são dados no barlake e mortos em cerimónias importantes, como funerais e a inauguração de casas sagradas (uma lulik). Em algumas zonas de arroz, os agricultores fazem tradicionalmente os búfalos andar pelos campos alagados para pisar e preparar a terra. O gado de Bali, as cabras e os porcos também são comuns, e quase todas as famílias criam galinhas. Os animais andam muitas vezes soltos, o que pode estragar culturas e árvores jovens, por isso as comunidades fazem regras sobre onde podem pastar.
text.en: The water buffalo (karau in Tetun) is the most valued farm animal in many parts of Timor-Leste. Buffalo are a sign of wealth: they are given in barlake and killed for important ceremonies such as funerals and the inauguration of sacred houses (uma lulik). In some rice areas farmers traditionally drive buffalo through flooded fields to trample and prepare the soil. Bali cattle, goats and pigs are also common, and most families keep chickens. Animals often roam freely, which can damage crops and young trees, so communities make rules about where they may graze.
text.id: Kerbau (karau dalam bahasa Tetun) adalah hewan ternak yang paling dihargai di banyak bagian Timor-Leste. Kerbau adalah tanda kekayaan: kerbau diberikan dalam barlake dan disembelih pada upacara penting seperti pemakaman dan peresmian rumah adat (uma lulik). Di beberapa daerah persawahan, petani secara tradisional menggiring kerbau melalui sawah yang tergenang untuk menginjak-injak dan mengolah tanah. Sapi bali, kambing, dan babi juga umum, dan sebagian besar keluarga memelihara ayam. Ternak sering dilepas bebas sehingga dapat merusak tanaman dan pohon muda, karena itu masyarakat membuat aturan tentang tempat ternak boleh merumput.

text.tet: Timór nia animál fuik barak raru no seidauk iha estudu barak. Ai-laran lakon, ahi ne'ebé han ai-laran, kasa ho asu no kaer manu no réptil atu fa'an mak perigu prinsipál sira. Área protejida hanesan Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana fó fatin seguru ba animál sira atu moris, no tara bandu bele bandu kasa iha ai-laran ida durante tinan balu. Ó bele ajuda: keta sosa animál fuik ka sira-nia na'an, hadook asu husi manu nia knuuk, no fó-hatene ba profesór ka lider lokál bainhira ó haree animál raru ida ka animál ida ne'ebé iha perigu.
text.pt: Muitos dos animais selvagens de Timor são raros e pouco estudados. A perda de floresta, os incêndios, a caça com cães e a captura de aves e répteis para venda são as principais ameaças. Áreas protegidas como o Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana dão aos animais lugares seguros para viver, e o tara bandu pode proibir a caça numa floresta durante vários anos. Pode ajudar não comprando animais selvagens nem a sua carne, mantendo os cães longe dos ninhos e avisando os professores ou os líderes locais quando vir um animal raro ou em perigo.
text.en: Many of Timor's wild animals are rare and little studied. Forest loss, fires, hunting with dogs and the capture of birds and reptiles for sale are the main threats. Protected areas such as Nino Konis Santana National Park give animals safe places to live, and tara bandu can ban hunting in a forest for several years. You can help by not buying wild animals or their meat, keeping dogs away from nests, and telling teachers or local leaders when you see a rare animal or an animal in danger.
text.id: Banyak satwa liar Timor yang langka dan belum banyak diteliti. Hilangnya hutan, kebakaran, perburuan dengan anjing, dan penangkapan burung serta reptil untuk dijual adalah ancaman utama. Kawasan lindung seperti Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana memberi tempat aman bagi satwa, dan tara bandu dapat melarang perburuan di suatu hutan selama beberapa tahun. Kamu dapat membantu dengan tidak membeli satwa liar atau dagingnya, menjauhkan anjing dari sarang, dan memberi tahu guru atau pemimpin setempat jika melihat satwa langka atau satwa yang dalam bahaya.

why.tet: Lekirauk la bele liu tasi kle'an rasik; karik ema mak lori mai. Lafaek, niki no manu bele nani ka semo.
why.pt: Os macacos não atravessam sozinhos mares profundos; provavelmente foram trazidos por pessoas. Crocodilos, morcegos e aves nadam ou voam.
why.en: Macaques cannot cross deep seas on their own and were probably brought by people; crocodiles, bats and birds can swim or fly.
why.id: Monyet tidak dapat menyeberangi laut dalam sendiri; kemungkinan dibawa manusia. Buaya, kelelawar, dan burung bisa berenang atau terbang.

why.tet: Niki bele semo no laho bele namlele iha ai-horis nia leten, tan ne'e sira to'o Timór uluk liu ema.
why.pt: Os morcegos voam e os ratos podem ser levados em jangadas de plantas, por isso chegaram a Timor antes das pessoas.
why.en: Bats can fly and rats can drift on rafts of plants, so they reached Timor long before people.
why.id: Kelelawar bisa terbang dan tikus bisa hanyut di atas rakit tumbuhan, sehingga keduanya tiba di Timor sebelum manusia.

review.notes: Origins of introduced mammals (deer from Java/Bali, macaque from the west, cuscus from the Moluccas, palm civet) follow general references and earlier Lafa text – check against recent archaeology (arrival dates). Timor monitor (Varanus timorensis) on Timor – check. Timor ponies shipped to Australia in the 19th century (Wikipedia 'Timor pony'). Buffalo trampling flooded rice fields is a traditional practice in some areas – check. The Tetun option for 'deer' in quiz 2 is a description. Tetun terms to check: laku (palm civet), lagartu, varanu Timór, mate-rate (funeral), sama (trample), ai-oan, dikur (horn), koelu, busa.

title.tet: Ai-laran no ai-horis sira: ai-kameli, ai-parapa no seluk tan
title.pt: Florestas e plantas: sândalo, mangais e outras
title.en: Forests and plants: sandalwood, mangroves and more
title.id: Hutan dan tumbuhan: cendana, bakau, dan lainnya

summary.tet: Timór nia ai-laran naturál oioin: husi ai-laran maran iha kosta to'o ai-laran malirin no kalohan barak iha foho aas sira. Uluk ai-kameli halo Timór famozu ba negosiante sira, maibé ema ko'a barak liu, to'o ai-kameli sai raru. Ai-parapa proteje kosta, no ai-bubur (eukaliptu) taka foho maran barak.
summary.pt: As florestas naturais de Timor vão das matas secas de monção, na costa, às florestas frescas e cheias de nevoeiro das altas montanhas. O sândalo tornou Timor famoso entre os comerciantes, mas foi tão cortado que se tornou raro. Os mangais protegem as costas e o eucalipto (ai-bubur) cobre muitas colinas secas.
summary.en: Timor's natural forests range from dry monsoon woods on the coast to cool, misty forests on the high mountains. Sandalwood once made Timor famous among traders, but it was cut so much that it became rare. Mangroves protect the coasts, and eucalyptus (ai-bubur) covers many dry hills.
summary.id: Hutan alami Timor beragam, dari hutan musim yang kering di pesisir sampai hutan pegunungan yang sejuk dan berkabut. Cendana dulu membuat Timor terkenal di kalangan pedagang, tetapi ditebang begitu banyak sehingga menjadi langka. Hutan bakau melindungi pantai, dan eukaliptus (ai-bubur) menutupi banyak bukit yang kering.

text.tet: Timór-Leste nia ai-horis naturál muda tuir udan no tuir aas. Iha kosta norte ne'ebé maran, ai-laran monsaun nian lakon ai-tahan barak iha tempu bailoron, no savana loke ho du'ut, akadiru no ai-hun balu iha fatin barak. Sul, ne'ebé bokon liu, iha ai-laran rai-tetuk nian ne'ebé aas no matak liu. Iha foho aas sira, ai-laran kalohan nian malirin no nakonu ho orkídea no ai-horis ki'ik seluk. Durante sékulu barak, ema loke rai barak ba agrikultura, tan ne'e ohin loron ai-laran tuan no mahar hela liuliu iha foho tun-sa'e, iha fatin lulik no iha área protejida, hanesan ai-laran Lore iha Lautein. WWF bolu rejiaun ne'e nia ai-laran naturál “ai-laran Timór no Wetar ne'ebé ai-tahan monu”.
text.pt: A vegetação natural de Timor-Leste muda com a chuva e a altitude. Na seca costa norte, as florestas de monção perdem muitas folhas na estação seca, e a savana aberta, com capim, palmeiras e árvores dispersas, é comum. O sul, mais húmido, tem florestas de baixa altitude mais altas e verdes. Nas altas montanhas, as florestas de nevoeiro, frescas, estão cheias de fetos, orquídeas e musgos. Ao longo dos séculos, grande parte da terra foi desbravada para a agricultura, por isso hoje a floresta antiga e densa sobrevive sobretudo em encostas íngremes, lugares sagrados e áreas protegidas, como a floresta de Lore, em Lautém. A WWF chama às florestas naturais da região «florestas caducifólias de Timor e Wetar».
text.en: Timor-Leste's natural vegetation changes with rain and height. On the dry north coast, monsoon forests lose many of their leaves in the dry season, and open savanna with grass, palms and scattered trees is common. The wetter south has taller, greener lowland forests. On the high mountains, cool cloud forests are full of ferns, orchids and mosses. Over centuries much of the land was cleared for farming, so today dense old forest survives mainly on steep slopes, in sacred places and in protected areas such as the Lore forest in Lautém. WWF calls the natural forests of the region the Timor and Wetar deciduous forests.
text.id: Vegetasi alami Timor-Leste berubah menurut curah hujan dan ketinggian. Di pantai utara yang kering, hutan musim menggugurkan banyak daunnya pada musim kemarau, dan sabana terbuka dengan rumput, palem, dan pohon yang tersebar umum dijumpai. Wilayah selatan yang lebih basah memiliki hutan dataran rendah yang lebih tinggi dan hijau. Di pegunungan tinggi, hutan awan yang sejuk penuh pakis, anggrek, dan lumut. Selama berabad-abad sebagian besar lahan dibuka untuk pertanian, sehingga kini hutan tua yang lebat terutama tersisa di lereng curam, tempat keramat, dan kawasan lindung seperti hutan Lore di Lautém. WWF menyebut hutan alami kawasan ini hutan gugur Timor dan Wetar.

heading.tet: Ai-kameli: ai-hun ne'ebé lori negosiante mai Timór
heading.pt: O sândalo: a árvore que trouxe os comerciantes a Timor
heading.en: Sandalwood: the tree that brought traders to Timor
heading.id: Cendana: pohon yang mendatangkan pedagang ke Timor

text.tet: Ai-kameli mutin (Santalum album) iha ai-klaran ne'ebé morin, no ema uza ba insensu, perfume, ai-moruk no halo estátua ai. Durante sékulu barak, uluk liu molok europeu sira to'o, negosiante husi Xina, Java no rai malaiu sira mai Timór ho ró atu sosa ai-kameli, no depois Portugál no Olanda kompete ba komérsiu ne'e. Ema ko'a barak liu, to'o iha sékulu 20 ai-kameli sai raru. Ohin loron komunidade, eskola no Governu kuda ai-kameli oan atu hamoris fali. Ai-kameli mak ai-horis parazita-balu: ninia abut kesi ba ai-horis seluk nia abut atu foti bee no hahán balu.
text.pt: O sândalo-branco (Santalum album, ai-kameli em tétum) tem um cerne perfumado usado em incenso, perfumes, medicamentos e escultura. Durante séculos, muito antes da chegada dos europeus, comerciantes chineses, javaneses e malaios navegaram até Timor para o comprar, e mais tarde portugueses e holandeses disputaram esse comércio. Foi tão cortado que, no século XX, o sândalo já se tinha tornado raro. Hoje comunidades, escolas e o Governo plantam sândalos jovens para o fazer voltar. O sândalo é uma planta semiparasita: as suas raízes ligam-se às raízes das plantas vizinhas para lhes tirar parte da água e do alimento.
text.en: White sandalwood (Santalum album, ai-kameli in Tetun) has a sweet-smelling heartwood used for incense, perfume, medicine and carving. For centuries, long before Europeans arrived, Chinese, Javanese and Malay traders sailed to Timor to buy it, and later the Portuguese and the Dutch competed for the trade. So much was cut that by the 20th century sandalwood had become rare. Today communities, schools and the Government plant young sandalwood trees to bring it back. A sandalwood tree is a half-parasite: its roots join the roots of nearby plants to take some of their water and food.
text.id: Cendana putih (Santalum album, ai-kameli dalam bahasa Tetun) memiliki teras kayu yang harum dan dipakai untuk dupa, minyak wangi, obat, dan ukiran. Selama berabad-abad, jauh sebelum orang Eropa datang, pedagang Tiongkok, Jawa, dan Melayu berlayar ke Timor untuk membelinya, lalu Portugis dan Belanda bersaing memperebutkan perdagangan itu. Pohon ini ditebang begitu banyak sehingga pada abad ke-20 cendana sudah langka. Kini masyarakat, sekolah, dan pemerintah menanam pohon cendana muda untuk memulihkannya. Cendana adalah tumbuhan setengah parasit: akarnya menempel pada akar tumbuhan di sekitarnya untuk mengambil sebagian air dan makanannya.

text.tet: Ai-parapa mak ai-hun ne'ebé moris iha rai-tahu masin entre rai no tasi, liuliu iha mota-ibun no baía kalma iha kosta rua, hanesan besik Metinaro no Hera iha kosta norte. Ninia abut ne'ebé kahur malu hamenus laloran, proteje tasi-ibun husi erozaun no anin-boot, no kaer rai-tahu. Ikan-oan, kadiuk no boek subar entre abut sira, no manu halo knuuk iha sanak sira. Ema ko'a ai-parapa barak ba ai-maran, ba harii uma no ba tanke ikan. Komunidade no eskola sira kuda fali ai-parapa, no ida-ne'e ajuda balu moris fali.
text.pt: Os mangais (ai-parapa) são árvores que crescem na lama salgada entre a terra e o mar, sobretudo em fozes de rios e baías calmas de ambas as costas, por exemplo perto de Metinaro e Hera, na costa norte. As suas raízes emaranhadas travam as ondas, protegem a costa da erosão e das tempestades e retêm a lama. Peixes jovens, caranguejos e camarões abrigam-se entre as raízes, e as aves fazem ninho nos ramos. Muitos mangais foram cortados para lenha, construção e tanques de peixe. A replantação feita por comunidades e escolas está a ajudar alguns a crescer de novo.
text.en: Mangroves (ai-parapa) are trees that grow in salty mud between land and sea, especially in river mouths and calm bays on both coasts, for example near Metinaro and Hera on the north coast. Their tangled roots slow down waves, protect the shore from erosion and storms, and trap mud. Young fish, crabs and shrimps shelter among the roots, and birds nest in the branches. Many mangroves have been cut for firewood, building and fish ponds. Replanting by communities and schools is helping some of them to grow back.
text.id: Bakau (ai-parapa) adalah pohon yang tumbuh di lumpur asin di antara daratan dan laut, terutama di muara sungai dan teluk yang tenang di kedua pantai, misalnya dekat Metinaro dan Hera di pantai utara. Akar-akarnya yang saling berkait memperlambat ombak, melindungi pantai dari abrasi dan badai, serta menahan lumpur. Ikan muda, kepiting, dan udang berlindung di antara akarnya, dan burung bersarang di dahannya. Banyak bakau ditebang untuk kayu bakar, bangunan, dan tambak. Penanaman kembali oleh masyarakat dan sekolah membantu sebagian bakau tumbuh lagi.

heading.tet: Ai-bubur, akadiru no ai-hun seluk ne'ebé iha uzu

text.tet: Eukaliptu espésie barak liu mai husi Austrália, maibé espésie rua, Eucalyptus alba no Eucalyptus urophylla, moris naturál iha Timór. Iha Tetun ema bolu sira ai-bubur, no sira taka foho maran no foho nia lolon barak, dala barak ho du'ut iha okos. Ai-horis tipu palmeira iha uzu barak: nu, no akadiru, ne'ebé ninia tahan ema uza atu kobre uma no halo luhu, no ninia been fó tua. Ai-hun importante seluk mak kami, sukaer, au no ai-hun aas ne'ebé ema kuda atu fó mahon ba kafé. Ema mós kuda ai-teka no mogno atu hetan ai ba uma no mobília.
text.pt: A maior parte dos eucaliptos é australiana, mas duas espécies, Eucalyptus alba e Eucalyptus urophylla, crescem naturalmente em Timor. Em tétum chamam-se ai-bubur, e cobrem muitas colinas secas e encostas de montanha, muitas vezes com capim por baixo. As palmeiras são muito úteis: o coqueiro (nu) e a palmeira lontar ou palmira (akadiru), cujas folhas servem para telhados e cestos e cuja seiva dá vinho de palma. Outras árvores importantes são a noz-de-vela (kami), o tamarindo (sukaer), o bambu (au) e as árvores altas de sombra plantadas para proteger o café. A teca e o mogno foram plantados para madeira.
text.en: Most eucalyptus trees are Australian, but two kinds, Eucalyptus alba and Eucalyptus urophylla, grow naturally on Timor. In Tetun they are called ai-bubur, and they cover many dry hills and mountain slopes, often with grass underneath. Palms are very useful: the coconut (nu), and the lontar or palmyra palm (akadiru), whose leaves are used for roofs and baskets and whose sap gives palm wine. Other important trees include candlenut (kami), tamarind (sukaer), bamboo (au) and the tall shade trees planted to protect coffee. Teak and mahogany have been planted for timber.
text.id: Sebagian besar pohon eukaliptus berasal dari Australia, tetapi dua jenis, Eucalyptus alba dan Eucalyptus urophylla, tumbuh alami di Timor. Dalam bahasa Tetun pohon ini disebut ai-bubur, dan menutupi banyak bukit kering dan lereng gunung, sering dengan rumput di bawahnya. Palem sangat berguna: kelapa (nu) dan lontar (akadiru), yang daunnya dipakai untuk atap dan keranjang serta niranya menghasilkan tuak. Pohon penting lainnya adalah kemiri (kami), asam (sukaer), bambu (au), dan pohon pelindung tinggi yang ditanam untuk menaungi kopi. Jati dan mahoni ditanam untuk diambil kayunya.

text.tet: Ai-horis fó ba família timoroan hahán, ai-moruk, sasán atu harii uma, ai-maran no sasán ba serimónia. Matan-dook sira uza ai-tahan, ai-abut no ai-kulit hanesan ai-moruk, no ema fahe malus no bua hanesan sinál simu vizitante. Família barak iha foho sei te'in ho ai-maran, no ida-ne'e hatodan ai-laran besik. Kuda ai-hun haleu uma, eskola no bee-matan, uza fogaun ne'ebé poupa ai, no proteje ai-laran lulik ajuda rai riku-soin matak ida-ne'e ba aban-bainrua.
text.pt: As plantas dão às famílias timorenses comida, remédios, materiais de construção, lenha e objetos para as cerimónias. Os curandeiros tradicionais usam folhas, raízes e cascas como remédio (ai-moruk), e a folha de bétel e a noz de areca (malus e bua) são partilhadas como sinal de boas-vindas. A maioria das famílias rurais ainda cozinha com lenha, o que pressiona as florestas próximas. Plantar árvores à volta das casas, escolas e nascentes, usar fogões que poupam lenha e proteger as florestas sagradas ajudam a guardar esta riqueza verde para o futuro.
text.en: Plants give Timorese families food, medicine, building materials, firewood and things for ceremonies. Traditional healers use leaves, roots and bark as medicine (ai-moruk), and betel leaf and areca nut (malus and bua) are shared as a sign of welcome. Most rural families still cook with firewood, which puts pressure on nearby forests. Planting trees around homes, schools and springs, using fuel-saving stoves, and protecting sacred forests help to keep this green wealth for the future.
text.id: Tumbuhan memberi keluarga Timor makanan, obat, bahan bangunan, kayu bakar, dan perlengkapan upacara. Penyembuh tradisional memakai daun, akar, dan kulit kayu sebagai obat (ai-moruk), dan daun sirih serta buah pinang (malus dan bua) dibagikan sebagai tanda penyambutan. Sebagian besar keluarga di pedesaan masih memasak dengan kayu bakar, sehingga menekan hutan di sekitarnya. Menanam pohon di sekitar rumah, sekolah, dan mata air, memakai tungku hemat kayu, dan melindungi hutan keramat membantu menjaga kekayaan hijau ini untuk masa depan.

title.pt: Áreas protegidas e o Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana
title.en: Protected areas and Nino Konis Santana National Park
title.id: Kawasan lindung dan Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana

summary.tet: Timór-Leste proteje fatin naturál espesiál sira tuir lei no tuir lisan. Ninia parke nasionál dahuluk, Nino Konis Santana, deklara iha 2007 iha nasaun nia rohan leste, no kobre maizumenus 1 236 km² rai no tasi. Parke ne'e proteje ai-laran, fatuk-kuak, Lagoa Ira Lalaro, tasi-le'un Jaku no ahu-ruin sira haleu Tutuala.
summary.pt: Timor-Leste protege lugares naturais especiais por lei e pelo costume. O seu primeiro parque nacional, o Nino Konis Santana, foi declarado em 2007 no extremo leste do país e cobre cerca de 1236 km² de terra e mar. Protege florestas, grutas, o lago Ira Lalaro, a ilha de Jaco e os recifes de coral à volta de Tutuala.
summary.en: Timor-Leste protects special natural places by law and by custom. Its first national park, Nino Konis Santana, was declared in 2007 at the eastern tip of the country and covers about 1,236 km² of land and sea. It protects forests, caves, Lake Ira Lalaro, Jaco Island and the coral reefs around Tutuala.
summary.id: Timor-Leste melindungi tempat-tempat alam yang istimewa melalui hukum dan adat. Taman nasional pertamanya, Nino Konis Santana, dinyatakan pada tahun 2007 di ujung timur negara ini dan mencakup sekitar 1.236 km² daratan dan laut. Taman ini melindungi hutan, gua, Danau Ira Lalaro, Pulau Jaco, dan terumbu karang di sekitar Tutuala.

text.tet: Área protejida mak fatin ida ne'ebé lei ka lisan tau matan ba natureza, atu ai-horis no animál sira bele moris, bee-matan sira hela moos, no ema bele uza no goza natureza ho kuidadu ba tempu naruk. Iha Timór-Leste, fatin protejida dahuluk sira tama iha lista iha 2000, iha ONU nia tranzisaun (UNTAET) nia tempu: área rai nian sanulu-resin-lima, inklui foho nia tutun, ai-laran ne'ebé sei hela, fatin bokon iha kosta, tasi-ibun no tasi-le'un Jaku. Iha 2016, Governu aprova Dekretu-Lei n.º 5/2016, ne'ebé harii sistema nasionál área protejida nian iha rai no iha tasi. Área protejida barak mós mak Área Importante ba Manu.
text.pt: Uma área protegida é um lugar onde a natureza é guardada pela lei ou pelo costume, para que plantas e animais possam viver, as fontes de água se mantenham limpas e as pessoas possam usar e apreciar a natureza com cuidado durante muito tempo. Em Timor-Leste, os primeiros lugares protegidos foram listados em 2000, durante a transição da ONU (UNTAET): quinze áreas terrestres, incluindo picos de montanha, restos de floresta, pântanos costeiros, praias e a ilha de Jaco. Em 2016, o Governo aprovou o Decreto-Lei n.º 5/2016, que criou um sistema nacional de áreas protegidas em terra e no mar. Muitas áreas protegidas são também Áreas Importantes para as Aves.
text.en: A protected area is a place where nature is kept safe by law or by custom, so that plants and animals can live, water sources stay clean, and people can use and enjoy nature carefully for a long time. In Timor-Leste, the first protected places were listed in 2000, during the UN transition (UNTAET): fifteen land areas including mountain peaks, forest remnants, coastal swamps, beaches and Jaco Island. In 2016 the Government approved Decree-Law No. 5/2016, which created a national system of protected areas on land and at sea. Many protected areas are also Important Bird Areas.
text.id: Kawasan lindung adalah tempat yang alamnya dijaga oleh hukum atau adat, agar tumbuhan dan hewan dapat hidup, sumber air tetap bersih, dan manusia dapat memanfaatkan serta menikmati alam dengan hati-hati untuk waktu yang lama. Di Timor-Leste, tempat-tempat lindung pertama ditetapkan pada tahun 2000, pada masa transisi PBB (UNTAET): lima belas kawasan darat, termasuk puncak gunung, sisa hutan, rawa pesisir, pantai, dan Pulau Jaco. Pada tahun 2016 Pemerintah mengesahkan Dekret-Undang-Undang No. 5/2016 yang membentuk sistem nasional kawasan lindung di darat dan di laut. Banyak kawasan lindung juga merupakan Daerah Penting bagi Burung.

text.tet: Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana kobre Timór nia rohan leste, iha munisípiu Lautein. Governu deklara parke ne'e iha 2007, nu'udar nasaun nia parke nasionál dahuluk. Ninia luan maizumenus ektare 123 600 (1 236 km²): maizumenus ektare 68 000 rai no ektare 55 600 tasi iha Triángulu Korál. Parke ne'e nia naran mai husi Nino Konis Santana, komandante FALINTIL husi rejiaun ne'e ne'ebé mate iha 1998. Parke ne'e liga Área Importante ba Manu tolu: Lore, Foho Paitchau ho Lagoa Ira Lalaro, no tasi-le'un Jaku. Iha 2025, Timór-Leste hatete katak nia prontu atu propoin parke ne'e ba UNESCO.
text.pt: O Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana cobre o extremo leste de Timor, no município de Lautém. Foi declarado em 2007 como o primeiro parque nacional do país. Tem cerca de 123 600 hectares (1236 km²): cerca de 68 000 hectares de terra e 55 600 hectares de mar no Triângulo de Coral. O parque tem o nome de Nino Konis Santana, comandante das FALINTIL desta região, que morreu em 1998. Liga três Áreas Importantes para as Aves: Lore, o monte Paitchau com o lago Ira Lalaro, e a ilha de Jaco. Em 2025, Timor-Leste anunciou que estava pronto para propor o parque à UNESCO.
text.en: Nino Konis Santana National Park covers the eastern tip of Timor, in the municipality of Lautém. It was declared in 2007 as the country's first national park. It covers about 123,600 hectares (1,236 km²): about 68,000 hectares of land and 55,600 hectares of sea in the Coral Triangle. The park is named after Nino Konis Santana, a FALINTIL commander from this region who died in 1998. It links three Important Bird Areas: Lore, Mount Paitchau with Lake Ira Lalaro, and Jaco Island. In 2025 Timor-Leste said it was ready to propose the park to UNESCO.
text.id: Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana mencakup ujung timur Timor, di munisipalitas Lautém. Taman ini dinyatakan pada tahun 2007 sebagai taman nasional pertama di negara ini. Luasnya sekitar 123.600 hektare (1.236 km²): sekitar 68.000 hektare daratan dan 55.600 hektare laut di Segitiga Terumbu Karang. Taman ini dinamai menurut Nino Konis Santana, komandan FALINTIL dari daerah ini yang meninggal pada tahun 1998. Taman ini menghubungkan tiga Daerah Penting bagi Burung: Lore, Gunung Paitchau bersama Danau Ira Lalaro, dan Pulau Jaco. Pada tahun 2025 Timor-Leste menyatakan siap mengusulkan taman ini ke UNESCO.

text.tet: Parke nia parte ne'ebé famozu liu mak tasi-le'un Jaku, illa ki'ik ida ne'ebé ema la hela, ho rai-henek mutin no ai-laran, iha Tutuala nia tasi, iha tasi-ibun Valu nia oin. Jaku lulik ba povu Fataluku: vizitante sira bele bá iha loron ho ró-na'in lokál sira, maibé tuir lisan, ema ida la toba iha ne'ebá. Iha fatuk aas sira besik Tutuala, fatuk-kuak hanesan Lene Hara no Ile Kére Kére iha pintura tuan iha fatuk, no ema uza ona fatuk-kuak balu tinan rihun sanulu resin liubá. Ahu-ruin sira haleu Jaku mak ida husi di'ak liu iha nasaun.
text.pt: A parte mais conhecida do parque é a ilha de Jaco, uma pequena ilha desabitada de areia branca e floresta, junto à costa de Tutuala, em frente à praia de Valu. Jaco é sagrada para o povo fataluku: os visitantes podem ir lá de dia com barqueiros locais, mas, por costume, ninguém passa a noite na ilha. Nas falésias perto de Tutuala, grutas e abrigos de calcário como Lene Hara e Ile Kére Kére guardam pinturas rupestres antigas, e algumas grutas foram usadas por pessoas há dezenas de milhares de anos. Os recifes de coral à volta de Jaco estão entre os mais saudáveis do país.
text.en: The best-known part of the park is Jaco Island, a small, uninhabited island of white sand and forest off the coast at Tutuala, across the water from Valu beach. Jaco is sacred to the Fataluku people: visitors may go there by day with local boatmen, but by custom nobody stays overnight. On the cliffs near Tutuala, limestone caves and rock shelters such as Lene Hara and Ile Kére Kére hold ancient rock paintings, and some caves were used by people tens of thousands of years ago. The coral reefs around Jaco are among the healthiest in the country.
text.id: Bagian taman yang paling terkenal adalah Pulau Jaco, pulau kecil tak berpenghuni berpasir putih dan berhutan di lepas pantai Tutuala, di seberang Pantai Valu. Jaco sakral bagi orang Fataluku: pengunjung boleh datang pada siang hari bersama tukang perahu setempat, tetapi menurut adat tidak ada yang bermalam di sana. Di tebing dekat Tutuala, gua dan ceruk batu kapur seperti Lene Hara dan Ile Kére Kére menyimpan lukisan batu kuno, dan beberapa gua sudah dipakai manusia puluhan ribu tahun lalu. Terumbu karang di sekitar Jaco termasuk yang paling sehat di negara ini.

text.tet: Iha rai, parke ne'e proteje ai-laran rai-tetuk nian balu ne'ebé boot liu ne'ebé sei hela iha Timór-Leste, iha planaltu fatuk-ahu ne'ebé sa'e ona, ho rai-kuak, fatuk-kuak no fatuk aas sira. Ai-laran sira-ne'e mak hela-fatin ba kakatua ho fulun kinur iha ulun, pombu sira ne'ebé han ai-fuan no manu seluk barak, no mós niki no réptil. Lagoa Ira Lalaro, lagoa boot liu iha nasaun, iha planaltu iha parke nia laran; ninia bee sa'e no tun tuir tempu, no tama ba rai okos. Família lokál sira kuda to'os, hakiak karau no kaer ikan iha parke laran, tan ne'e parke ne'e jere hamutuk ho komunidade, la'ós ho dada sai ema.
text.pt: Em terra, o parque protege algumas das maiores florestas de baixa altitude que restam em Timor-Leste, num planalto de calcário levantado, com sumidouros, grutas e falésias. Estas florestas abrigam a catatua-de-crista-amarela, pombos-da-fruta e muitas outras aves, além de morcegos e répteis. O lago Ira Lalaro, o maior do país, fica no planalto, dentro do parque; o nível da água muda com as estações e a água escoa por baixo da terra. As famílias locais cultivam a terra, criam búfalos e pescam dentro do parque, por isso este é gerido em conjunto com as comunidades, e não afastando as pessoas.
text.en: On land, the park protects some of the largest remaining lowland forests in Timor-Leste, on a raised limestone plateau with sinkholes, caves and cliffs. These forests are home to the yellow-crested cockatoo, fruit pigeons and many other birds, as well as bats and reptiles. Lake Ira Lalaro, the largest lake in the country, lies on the plateau inside the park; its water level changes with the seasons and the water drains underground. Local families farm, raise buffalo and fish within the park, so it is managed together with communities rather than by keeping people out.
text.id: Di darat, taman ini melindungi sebagian hutan dataran rendah terbesar yang masih tersisa di Timor-Leste, di dataran tinggi batu kapur yang terangkat dengan dolina, gua, dan tebing. Hutan ini menjadi rumah bagi kakatua jambul kuning, merpati buah, dan banyak burung lain, serta kelelawar dan reptil. Danau Ira Lalaro, danau terbesar di negara ini, terletak di dataran tinggi di dalam taman; ketinggian airnya berubah menurut musim dan airnya mengalir ke bawah tanah. Keluarga setempat bertani, memelihara kerbau, dan menangkap ikan di dalam taman, sehingga taman ini dikelola bersama masyarakat, bukan dengan mengusir orang.

text.tet: Área protejida la'o di'ak liu bainhira ema lokál sira apoia. Iha parke no iha fatin seluk, komunidade sira uza tara bandu, akordu lisan nian ne'ebé sira hametin iha serimónia ida, atu bandu ko'a ai, kasa ka kaer ikan iha fatin balu durante tempu balu, ho multa ne'ebé lisan hatuur. Conservation International ajuda komunidade sira iha Atauru no fatin seluk atu harii área tasi protejida ne'ebé komunidade jere. Ekoturizmu — haree manu, selam, vizita fatuk-kuak no uma-hospedajen komunidade nian iha Valu no Tutuala — lori rendimentu no tau matan ba natureza. Vizitante sira tenke tuir regra lokál, lori sira-nia lixu fila, no husu lisensa molok tama fatin lulik.
text.pt: As áreas protegidas funcionam melhor quando a população local as apoia. No parque e noutros lugares, as comunidades usam o tara bandu, um acordo tradicional selado numa cerimónia, para proibir durante algum tempo o corte de árvores, a caça ou a pesca em certos lugares, com multas fixadas pelo costume. A Conservation International ajudou comunidades de Ataúro e de outros lugares a criar áreas marinhas protegidas geridas localmente. O ecoturismo — observação de aves, mergulho, visitas a grutas e casas de hóspedes comunitárias em Valu e Tutuala — traz rendimento e mantém a natureza saudável. Os visitantes devem seguir as regras locais, levar o lixo consigo e pedir licença antes de entrar em lugares sagrados.
text.en: Protected areas work best when local people support them. In the park and elsewhere, communities use tara bandu, a customary agreement sealed in a ceremony, to ban cutting trees, hunting or fishing in certain places for a time, with penalties set by custom. Conservation International has helped communities on Ataúro and elsewhere to set up locally managed marine protected areas. Ecotourism — birdwatching, diving, visits to caves and community guesthouses at Valu and Tutuala — brings income while keeping nature healthy. Visitors should follow local rules, take their rubbish away and ask permission before entering sacred places.
text.id: Kawasan lindung berhasil jika didukung masyarakat setempat. Di taman ini dan di tempat lain, masyarakat memakai tara bandu, kesepakatan adat yang dikukuhkan dalam upacara, untuk melarang sementara penebangan pohon, perburuan, atau penangkapan ikan di tempat tertentu, dengan denda yang ditetapkan adat. Conservation International membantu masyarakat di Ataúro dan tempat lain membentuk kawasan konservasi laut yang dikelola setempat. Ekowisata — pengamatan burung, menyelam, kunjungan ke gua, dan penginapan milik masyarakat di Valu dan Tutuala — memberi penghasilan sambil menjaga alam tetap sehat. Pengunjung harus mematuhi aturan setempat, membawa pulang sampahnya, dan meminta izin sebelum memasuki tempat keramat.

title.tet: Dezafiu meiu-ambiente no konservasaun (tara bandu)
title.pt: Desafios ambientais e conservação (tara bandu)
title.en: Environmental challenges and conservation (tara bandu)
title.id: Tantangan lingkungan dan konservasi (tara bandu)

summary.tet: Timór-Leste hasoru problema meiu-ambiente boot sira: ai-laran lakon, erozaun rai, lixu plástiku no mudansa klimátika nia efeitu. Konstituisaun fó ba ema hotu-hotu direitu atu moris iha meiu-ambiente di'ak no devér atu proteje nia. Komunidade sira mós uza tara bandu, bandu tradisionál ida, atu tau matan ba ai-laran, bee no tasi.
summary.pt: Timor-Leste enfrenta problemas ambientais sérios: perda de floresta, erosão do solo, lixo de plástico e os efeitos das alterações climáticas. A Constituição dá a todos o direito a um ambiente saudável e o dever de o proteger. As comunidades usam também o tara bandu, uma proibição tradicional, para cuidar das florestas, da água e do mar.
summary.en: Timor-Leste faces serious environmental problems: forest loss, soil erosion, plastic waste and the effects of climate change. The Constitution gives everyone the right to a healthy environment and the duty to protect it. Communities also use tara bandu, a customary ban, to look after forests, water and the sea.
summary.id: Timor-Leste menghadapi masalah lingkungan yang serius: hilangnya hutan, erosi tanah, sampah plastik, dan dampak perubahan iklim. Konstitusi memberi setiap orang hak atas lingkungan yang sehat dan kewajiban untuk melindunginya. Masyarakat juga memakai tara bandu, larangan adat, untuk menjaga hutan, air, dan laut.

text.tet: Iha sékulu ikus ne'e, Timór-Leste lakon ninia ai-laran barak. Ema ko'a ai-hun ba ai-kameli no ai ba uma, loke rai ba kafé no to'os, sunu ai-laran durante tinan funu nian, no ko'a ai ba ai-maran, ne'ebé família barak iha foho sei uza atu te'in. Lere no sunu rai ba to'os, no ahi iha tempu bailoron ne'ebé halai ba ai-laran, hamate ai-oan tinan-tinan, no animál ne'ebé la'o livre han ai-oan sira. Bainhira ai-laran lakon, bee-matan sai maran, animál fuik lakon sira-nia hela-fatin, no rai sai manas no maran liu. Kampaña kuda ai-hun no agrofloresta, ne'ebé kahur ai-hun ho to'os, ajuda iha fatin balu.
text.pt: No último século, Timor-Leste perdeu grande parte da sua floresta. As árvores foram cortadas para sândalo e madeira, abatidas para café e outras culturas, queimadas durante anos de conflito e cortadas para lenha, que a maioria das famílias rurais ainda usa para cozinhar. A agricultura de corte e queimada e os incêndios da estação seca que escapam para o mato destroem árvores jovens todos os anos, e os animais soltos comem as plantas novas. Quando as florestas desaparecem, as nascentes secam, os animais selvagens perdem a casa e a terra fica mais quente e seca. As campanhas de plantação de árvores e a agrofloresta, que mistura árvores com culturas, estão a ajudar em alguns lugares.
text.en: Over the last century Timor-Leste has lost much of its forest. Trees were cut for sandalwood and timber, cleared for coffee and crops, burned during years of conflict, and cut for firewood, which most rural families still use for cooking. Slash-and-burn farming and dry-season fires that escape into the bush destroy young trees every year, and free-roaming animals eat seedlings. When forests disappear, springs dry up, wild animals lose their homes and the land becomes hotter and drier. Tree-planting campaigns and agroforestry, which mixes trees with crops, are helping in some places.
text.id: Selama satu abad terakhir Timor-Leste kehilangan sebagian besar hutannya. Pohon ditebang untuk cendana dan kayu, dibuka untuk kopi dan tanaman lain, dibakar selama tahun-tahun konflik, dan ditebang untuk kayu bakar, yang masih dipakai sebagian besar keluarga di pedesaan untuk memasak. Pertanian tebas-bakar dan kebakaran musim kemarau yang menjalar ke semak membinasakan pohon muda setiap tahun, dan ternak yang dilepas memakan bibit. Jika hutan hilang, mata air mengering, satwa liar kehilangan rumah, dan tanah menjadi lebih panas dan kering. Gerakan menanam pohon dan wanatani, yang memadukan pohon dengan tanaman pangan, membantu di beberapa tempat.

text.tet: Timór-Leste iha foho tun-sa'e makaas, rai mihis no udan boot iha tempu udan. Iha fatin ne'ebé ema hasai ona ai-hun no du'ut, udan lori rai di'ak iha leten ba bee. Erozaun ne'e halo to'os sai kiak liu, hakonu mota ho rai-tahu, halo inundasaun no rai-halai, no lori rai-tahu ba tasi, fatin ne'ebé nia taka ahu-ruin. Agrikultór sira bele hamenus erozaun: kuda tuir foho nia liña (kontornu), halo terrasu ki'ik no lutu fatuk, husik to'os nia restu iha rai leten, no kuda ai-hun no du'ut iha rai ne'ebé tun-sa'e liu.
text.pt: Timor-Leste tem encostas íngremes, solos finos e chuvas fortes na estação das chuvas. Onde se tiraram as árvores e o capim, a chuva arrasta a camada fértil do solo. Esta erosão empobrece os campos, enche os rios de lama, causa cheias e deslizamentos e leva lama para o mar, onde sufoca os recifes de coral. Os agricultores podem reduzir a erosão plantando segundo as curvas de nível, construindo pequenos socalcos e muros de pedra, deixando os restos das culturas no chão e plantando árvores e capins nos terrenos mais íngremes.
text.en: Timor-Leste has steep slopes, thin soils and heavy rain in the wet season. Where trees and grass have been removed, rain washes the topsoil away. This erosion makes fields poorer, fills rivers with mud, causes floods and landslides, and carries mud to the sea, where it smothers coral reefs. Farmers can reduce erosion by planting along the contour of the hill, building small terraces and stone walls, leaving crop waste on the ground, and planting trees and grasses on the steepest land.
text.id: Timor-Leste memiliki lereng curam, tanah yang tipis, dan hujan lebat pada musim hujan. Di tempat pohon dan rumput telah hilang, hujan menghanyutkan lapisan tanah atas. Erosi ini membuat ladang makin miskin hara, memenuhi sungai dengan lumpur, menyebabkan banjir dan longsor, serta membawa lumpur ke laut, tempat lumpur itu menutupi terumbu karang. Petani dapat mengurangi erosi dengan menanam mengikuti garis kontur bukit, membuat teras kecil dan pagar batu, membiarkan sisa tanaman di tanah, serta menanam pohon dan rumput di lahan yang paling curam.

text.tet: Bainhira sidade sira sai boot, lixu mós aumenta. Iha Dili, saku plástiku, botir no hahán nia embalajen taka valeta, halo inundasaun aat liu, no udan boot lori sira ba tasi, to'o iha tasi-ibun no iha lenuk no ikan nia kabun. Sunu plástiku halo ahi-suar ne'ebé iha venenu. Halibur lixu ho di'ak liu, resikla, uza plástiku uza-dala-ida menus, no nunka soe lixu ba mota ka tasi mak pasu importante sira. Eskola, grupu joventude no uma-kreda barak organiza loron hamoos iha tasi-ibun no iha bairru sira.
text.pt: À medida que as cidades crescem, cresce também o lixo. Em Díli, sacos de plástico, garrafas e embalagens entopem os esgotos, agravam as cheias e são levados para o mar depois das chuvas fortes, acabando nas praias e no estômago de tartarugas e peixes. Queimar plástico liberta fumo tóxico. Melhorar a recolha do lixo, reciclar, usar menos plástico descartável e nunca deitar lixo nos rios ou no mar são passos importantes. Muitas escolas, grupos de jovens e igrejas organizam dias de limpeza nas praias e nos bairros.
text.en: As towns grow, so does rubbish. In Dili, plastic bags, bottles and food wrappers block drains, make floods worse and wash into the sea after heavy rain, ending up on beaches and in the stomachs of turtles and fish. Burning plastic releases toxic smoke. Better waste collection, recycling, using fewer single-use plastics, and never throwing rubbish into rivers or the sea are important steps. Many schools, youth groups and churches organise clean-up days on beaches and in neighbourhoods.
text.id: Seiring tumbuhnya kota, sampah juga bertambah. Di Dili, kantong plastik, botol, dan bungkus makanan menyumbat saluran, memperparah banjir, dan hanyut ke laut setelah hujan lebat, lalu berakhir di pantai dan di perut penyu serta ikan. Membakar plastik menghasilkan asap beracun. Pengumpulan sampah yang lebih baik, daur ulang, mengurangi plastik sekali pakai, dan tidak pernah membuang sampah ke sungai atau laut adalah langkah penting. Banyak sekolah, kelompok pemuda, dan gereja mengadakan hari bersih-bersih di pantai dan lingkungan tempat tinggal.

text.tet: Mudansa klimátika afeta ona Timór-Leste. Temperatura sa'e, udan sai susar liu atu hatene oin, no udan boot hanesan iha Abríl 2021 halo estragu barak liu. Tasi nia nível ne'ebé sa'e no laloran makaas liu han tasi-ibun no ameasa estrada no aldeia sira iha kosta, no tasi ne'ebé manas liu estraga ahu-ruin. Timór-Leste halo gás efeitu-estufa uitoan tebes kompara ho mundu, maibé nia vulneravel tebes tanba ninia rai tun-sa'e, ninia agrikultura depende ba udan, no ninia komunidade barak iha kosta. Adapta katak proteje ai-laran no ai-parapa, poupa bee, uza fini ne'ebé moris maski bee menus, no harii estrada no uma ne'ebé forte liu.
text.pt: As alterações climáticas já afetam Timor-Leste. As temperaturas estão a subir, as chuvas são cada vez menos previsíveis e as chuvadas fortes, como as de abril de 2021, causam mais estragos. A subida do nível do mar e as ondas mais fortes desgastam as praias e ameaçam estradas e aldeias costeiras, e os mares mais quentes prejudicam os recifes de coral. Timor-Leste produz muito pouco dos gases com efeito de estufa do mundo, mas é muito vulnerável por causa do terreno íngreme, da dependência da agricultura de sequeiro e das muitas comunidades costeiras. Adaptar-se significa proteger florestas e mangais, poupar água, usar sementes resistentes à seca e construir estradas e casas mais fortes.
text.en: Climate change is already affecting Timor-Leste. Temperatures are rising, rains are becoming less predictable, and heavy downpours like those of April 2021 cause more damage. Rising sea levels and stronger waves erode beaches and threaten coastal roads and villages, and warmer seas harm coral reefs. Timor-Leste produces very little of the world's greenhouse gases, but it is very vulnerable because of its steep land, its dependence on rain-fed farming and its many coastal communities. Adapting means protecting forests and mangroves, saving water, using drought-tolerant seeds and building stronger roads and houses.
text.id: Perubahan iklim sudah memengaruhi Timor-Leste. Suhu meningkat, hujan makin sulit diperkirakan, dan hujan deras seperti pada April 2021 menimbulkan kerusakan lebih besar. Kenaikan permukaan laut dan ombak yang lebih kuat mengikis pantai serta mengancam jalan dan desa pesisir, dan laut yang lebih hangat merusak terumbu karang. Timor-Leste hanya menghasilkan sangat sedikit gas rumah kaca dunia, tetapi sangat rentan karena lahannya curam, bergantung pada pertanian tadah hujan, dan memiliki banyak komunitas pesisir. Beradaptasi berarti melindungi hutan dan bakau, menghemat air, memakai benih tahan kekeringan, serta membangun jalan dan rumah yang lebih kuat.

heading.tet: Lei no lisan: Artigu 61 no tara bandu
heading.pt: Lei e costume: o artigo 61.º e o tara bandu
heading.en: Law and custom: Article 61 and tara bandu
heading.id: Hukum dan adat: Pasal 61 dan tara bandu

text.tet: Konstituisaun nia Artigu 61 dehan katak ema hotu-hotu iha direitu atu moris iha ambiente ne'ebé moos, nabelun-di'ak ho natureza, no iha devér atu proteje nia ba jerasaun aban-bainrua nian; Artigu 139 hatutan katak tenke uza rekursu naturál sira la ho estraga ekosistema. Iha 2012 Governu aprova Lei-Baze Ambiente nian (Dekretu-Lei n.º 26/2012). Hamutuk ho lei, komunidade sira hamoris fali tara bandu, ne'ebé ema labele halo durante okupasaun. Iha serimónia públiku ida ne'ebé katuas sira no lia-na'in lidera, komunidade konkorda bandu ida — hanesan bandu ko'a ai besik bee-matan, kasa, ka kaer ikan iha ahu-ruin — no tara sinál ida iha ai-riin. Ema ne'ebé viola bandu ne'e selu multa tuir lisan.
text.pt: O artigo 61.º da Constituição diz que todos têm direito a um ambiente sadio e ecologicamente equilibrado e o dever de o proteger para as gerações futuras; o artigo 139.º acrescenta que os recursos naturais devem ser aproveitados sem destruir os ecossistemas. Em 2012 o Governo aprovou a Lei de Bases do Ambiente (Decreto-Lei n.º 26/2012). A par da lei, as comunidades fizeram renascer o tara bandu, que tinha sido reprimido durante a ocupação. Numa cerimónia pública conduzida pelos anciãos e pelo lia-na'in, a comunidade acorda uma proibição — por exemplo, de cortar árvores perto de uma nascente, caçar ou pescar num recife — e pendura um sinal num poste. Quem a quebrar paga uma multa fixada pelo costume.
text.en: Article 61 of the Constitution says that everyone has the right to a healthy environment in balance with nature and the duty to protect it for future generations; Article 139 adds that natural resources must be used without destroying ecosystems. In 2012 the Government approved the Environmental Basic Law (Decree-Law No. 26/2012). Alongside the law, communities revived tara bandu, which had been suppressed during the occupation. In a public ceremony led by elders and the lia-na'in, a community agrees a ban — for example on cutting trees near a spring, hunting, or fishing on a reef — and hangs a sign on a post. Anyone who breaks it pays a fine set by custom.
text.id: Pasal 61 Konstitusi menyatakan bahwa setiap orang berhak atas lingkungan yang sehat dan seimbang dengan alam serta wajib melindunginya untuk generasi mendatang; Pasal 139 menambahkan bahwa sumber daya alam harus dimanfaatkan tanpa merusak ekosistem. Pada tahun 2012 Pemerintah mengesahkan Undang-Undang Dasar Lingkungan (Dekret-UU No. 26/2012). Di samping hukum negara, masyarakat menghidupkan kembali tara bandu, yang ditekan pada masa pendudukan. Dalam upacara terbuka yang dipimpin para tetua dan lia-na'in, masyarakat menyepakati suatu larangan — misalnya menebang pohon di dekat mata air, berburu, atau menangkap ikan di terumbu — lalu menggantungkan tanda pada sebuah tiang. Siapa pun yang melanggar membayar denda menurut adat.

q.tet: Ita tenke halo saida ho lixu plástiku?
q.pt: O que se deve fazer com o lixo de plástico?
q.en: What should you do with plastic rubbish?
q.id: Apa yang harus dilakukan dengan sampah plastik?

options.tet: Sunu iha eskola nia sala laran
Tau iha lixu-fatin ka rai atu resikla
options.pt: Pô-lo no caixote do lixo ou guardá-lo para reciclar
options.en: Put it in a bin or keep it for recycling
options.id: Membuangnya ke tempat sampah atau menyimpannya untuk didaur ulang

why.tet: Plástiku ne'ebé ema soe ba mota to'o tasi no oho lenuk no ikan; sunu plástiku halo ahi-suar ho venenu.
why.pt: O plástico deitado aos rios chega ao mar e mata tartarugas e peixes; queimá-lo liberta fumo tóxico.
why.en: Plastic thrown into rivers reaches the sea and kills turtles and fish; burning it releases toxic smoke.
why.id: Plastik yang dibuang ke sungai sampai ke laut dan membunuh penyu dan ikan; membakarnya menghasilkan asap beracun.

q.tet: Konstituisaun uza liafuan Tetun saida ba “ambiente” ne'ebé haleu ita?
q.pt: Que palavra tétum usa a Constituição para «ambiente»?
q.en: What is the Tetun word for environment used in the Constitution?
q.id: Kata Tetun apa yang dipakai Konstitusi untuk “lingkungan”?

why.tet: Konstituisaun nia Artigu 61 naran “Meiu-ambiente”.
why.pt: O artigo 61.º da Constituição, em tétum, chama-se «Meiu-ambiente».
why.en: Article 61 of the Constitution is called “Meiu-ambiente” in Tetun.
why.id: Pasal 61 Konstitusi dalam bahasa Tetun berjudul “Meiu-ambiente”.

q.tet: Erozaun rai mak saida?
q.pt: O que é a erosão do solo?
q.en: What is soil erosion?
q.id: Apa itu erosi tanah?

options.tet: Bee ka anin lori rai ba
options.pt: O solo ser arrastado pela água ou pelo vento
options.en: Soil being washed or blown away

options.pt: A chuva a cair no mar
O mar a ficar mais salgado

why.tet: Bainhira la iha ai-hun no du'ut, udan lori rai di'ak ba mota no tasi; ida-ne'e mak erozaun.
why.pt: Sem árvores nem capim, a chuva leva o solo fértil para os rios e o mar: isso é erosão.
why.en: Without trees and grass, rain carries fertile soil into rivers and the sea: that is erosion.
why.id: Tanpa pohon dan rumput, hujan membawa tanah subur ke sungai dan laut: itulah erosi.

q.tet: Se mak baibain lidera serimónia tara bandu?
q.pt: Quem conduz normalmente uma cerimónia de tara bandu?
q.en: Who usually leads a tara bandu ceremony?
q.id: Siapa yang biasanya memimpin upacara tara bandu?

why.tet: Lia-na'in mak autoridade lisan nian; nia no katuas sira lidera serimónia no hatuur bandu no multa.
why.pt: O lia-na'in é a autoridade do direito costumeiro; com os anciãos, conduz a cerimónia e fixa as proibições e multas.
why.en: The lia-na'in is the customary-law authority; with the elders, he leads the ceremony and sets the bans and fines.
why.id: Lia-na'in adalah pemangku hukum adat; bersama para tetua ia memimpin upacara dan menetapkan larangan serta denda.

q.tet: Artigu saida husi Timór-Leste nia Konstituisaun mak ko'alia kona-ba meiu-ambiente?
q.pt: Que artigo da Constituição de Timor-Leste trata do ambiente?
q.en: Which article of the Constitution of Timor-Leste is about the environment?
q.id: Pasal berapa dalam Konstitusi Timor-Leste yang mengatur lingkungan?

why.tet: Artigu 61 fó direitu ba meiu-ambiente di'ak no devér atu proteje; Artigu 139 ko'alia kona-ba rekursu naturál.
why.pt: O artigo 61.º dá o direito a um ambiente sadio e o dever de o proteger; o artigo 139.º trata dos recursos naturais.
why.en: Article 61 gives the right to a healthy environment and the duty to protect it; Article 139 deals with natural resources.
why.id: Pasal 61 memberi hak atas lingkungan yang sehat dan kewajiban melindunginya; Pasal 139 mengatur sumber daya alam.

q.tet: Tanba saida Timór-Leste vulneravel tebes ba mudansa klimátika maski nia halo gás efeitu-estufa uitoan?
q.pt: Porque é que Timor-Leste é muito vulnerável às alterações climáticas, apesar de emitir poucos gases com efeito de estufa?
q.en: Why is Timor-Leste very vulnerable to climate change even though it emits little greenhouse gas?
q.id: Mengapa Timor-Leste sangat rentan terhadap perubahan iklim meskipun hanya menghasilkan sedikit gas rumah kaca?

options.en: It is near the North Pole

options.tet: Rai tun-sa'e, agrikultura depende ba udan no komunidade barak iha kosta
options.pt: Terreno íngreme, agricultura dependente da chuva e muitas comunidades costeiras
options.en: Steep land, rain-fed farming and many coastal communities
options.id: Lahan curam, pertanian tadah hujan, dan banyak komunitas pesisir

options.pt: Os seus vulcões estão em erupção

why.tet: Udan boot no seka afeta direta foho tun-sa'e, to'os ne'ebé depende ba udan no aldeia iha kosta.
why.pt: Chuvas fortes e secas afetam diretamente as encostas íngremes, as culturas dependentes da chuva e as aldeias costeiras.
why.en: Heavy rain and drought directly hit steep slopes, rain-fed crops and coastal villages.
why.id: Hujan lebat dan kekeringan langsung memengaruhi lereng curam, pertanian tadah hujan, dan desa pesisir.
